brief.language: English or none - the engine decides with the audio mode
brief.objective: Introduce the character to a cold viewer in 12 seconds in a public setting so that the character's energy, rule and silhouette are legible muted; make the viewer want to see the next one. This is a bake-off: the same brief runs for three characters and the owner compares the rendered tests.
constraints: Public setting from the bible's recurring locations; generic blurred passers-by allowed, never the joke.
Render tier: draft_mini (one 12 s Seedance 2.0 Mini unit, <=15 s, one generation unit, at most one cut) - this is a cost-capped test render.
The bible rule must land inside 12 seconds; the signature gesture may be used once.
Any dance or move is original and fully described; no trending dance or sound.
negative_constraints: Do not copy any researched creator's look, catchphrase or footage.
No readable brand text in frame.
No real people or recognisable locations.

premises.logline: Outside a corner shop, Uncle Verdict unfolds his chair and scores a closed umbrella 2 out of 10; rain arrives from the top edge, a dry stranger's umbrella drifts past, and he turns the dial down to 1.
premises.audience_emotion: Delighted exasperation: the viewer sees the rain before he admits it and itches to argue in the comments.
premises.character_desire: To be the final authority on umbrellas, today.
premises.obstacle: The rain and the plainly useful umbrella in the background contradict him in frame.
premises.escalation: Verdict at 2, first drops on the paddle, a generic passer-by's open umbrella slides through the frame edge, dial goes lower to 1.
premises.surprise: He does not move, shelter or blink; the rain lands on his bald crown and the serenity does not change.
premises.payoff: He turns the dial with one finger, holds the paddle to the lens, and says: 'Umbrella. Two out of ten. Correct answer: a tiny roof for nobody.' Rain pours, a dry umbrella passes, he lowers the dial to 1: 'Final.'
premises.structure: Rule-complete single beat: claim, evidence enters, doubling down, hold on the face.
premises.why_send_it: Sent to the friend who always argues about umbrellas with the message 'this is you'; the wrong take invites a reply.
premises.commercial_fit: None needed; no brands. Umbrellas are a universal object and suit sponsor-safe categories later.

production_format.camera_style: Locked-off phone at seated eye level, centred portrait; rain and the passing umbrella enter from the frame edges.
production_format.rationale: The cleanest cold-viewer introduction: static portrait shows silhouette, the verdict format and the rule within one generation unit, with the quiet delivery doing the work. Revised 2026-10-08: one hard cut hides the dial change (state 2 -> cut -> state 1), per platform hand-object staging rules.

premises.logline: In a laundrette window seat, Uncle Verdict scores a warm folded towel zero out of ten while a slow push-in reveals the dryer door swinging open and fresh towels spilling over his loafers.
premises.audience_emotion: Cosy absurdity with a slow-burn laugh at the pile building up.
premises.character_desire: To rule that towels are a failure.
premises.obstacle: Warm, clean, plainly excellent towels keep arriving in frame.
premises.escalation: Towel handed down from the edge, door pops, pile reaches his shoe, the dial already at 0 has nowhere lower so he taps the paddle itself as if the dial were broken.
premises.surprise: He treats the dial's floor as the world's fault.
premises.payoff: Voice-over: 'Towel. Zero out of ten. Correct answer: a sad flat blanket.' He turns the dial the wrong way, holds up the paddle, 'Final.'
premises.structure: Slow reveal; the camera finds the evidence while the voice stays certain.
premises.why_send_it: Sent to the flatmate who folds towels wrong, with the caption 'rate this'.
premises.commercial_fit: Laundry categories are generic; no brand text in frame.
premises.rejected_because: the dial floor makes the rule's wrong-direction step weaker than P1

production_format.camera_style: Slow motivated push-in from window height to his face, steam and dryer drum glow as practical light.
production_format.rationale: Moves the show to a second recurring location and voice-over so mouth sync is not a risk in a cheap render; the push-in motivates the reveal.

premises.logline: On a park bench row, Uncle Verdict rates a paper cup of tea 10 out of 10 in a main shot; one cutaway insert shows the tea is cold with a leaf floating in it, and he turns the dial up to 10 anyway.
premises.audience_emotion: Smug disbelief; the insert lets the viewer feel superior to him.
premises.character_desire: To crown tea the best thing on earth.
premises.obstacle: The insert shows still, cold, leaf-dotted tea.
premises.escalation: Verdict 8, cut to insert, back to the main shot with 10.
premises.surprise: The insert shows what the camera knows and he does not.
premises.payoff: Text: 'Tea. Eight out of ten. Correct answer: warm water in a hurry.' After the insert he turns the dial up and holds up the paddle: 'Final.'
premises.structure: Main shot plus insert (the one allowed cut); evidence before the character sees it.
premises.why_send_it: Sent to the tea-obsessed sibling with 'you in a nutshell'.
premises.commercial_fit: Tea is a universal object; no brand shown.
premises.rejected_because: the insert spends the one cut and the caption-only delivery makes the character less warm than a spoken take

production_format.camera_style: Locked medium main shot plus a single macro insert of the cup.
production_format.rationale: Silent text option tests whether the character reads without any voice; the insert proves the evidence-before-him rule visually.

premises.logline: Outside the corner shop, an unseen friend behind the phone asks Uncle Verdict about a banana; he scores it 4 out of 10, a hand from frame edge holds up a perfect one, and he lowers the dial to 2.
premises.audience_emotion: Warm, conversational comedy; the viewer feels like the third person in the chat.
premises.character_desire: To be asked, and to answer with authority.
premises.obstacle: The friend's spotless banana contradicts the score.
premises.escalation: Question, verdict, banana offered, verdict lowered.
premises.surprise: The off-camera voice stays kind and never mocks him.
premises.payoff: Friend: 'And the banana?' Uncle: 'Banana. Four out of ten. Correct answer: a yellow apology.' The banana is perfect; he turns the dial down to 2, holds the paddle to the lens: 'Final.'
premises.structure: Question-and-answer exchange with a visible object as evidence.
premises.why_send_it: Sent to a family member who has strong food opinions.
premises.commercial_fit: Fruit is generic; no brand text.
premises.rejected_because: off-camera voice dilutes the solo seated stillness and adds a second voice to a 12 s clip

production_format.camera_style: Handheld phone at seated eye level, held by the friend, with slight settle; the friend's hand enters from an edge.
production_format.rationale: Adds a relationship and a second voice to test whether the character holds a two-person beat in one cheap unit.

premises.logline: Silent loop in a laundrette window seat: a leaf blows past, Uncle Verdict dials a verdict on the leaf, and the clip ends on the same empty-chair pose it opened with.
premises.audience_emotion: Hypnotic calm; the loop invites a second watch.
premises.obstacle: The leaf keeps coming back and he keeps reappraising it.
premises.escalation: Dial moves one notch each pass until the loop closes.
premises.surprise: The last frame equals the first, so the verdict starts again.
premises.payoff: He turns the dial, holds the paddle to the lens in silence, and the frame returns to where it began.
premises.structure: Loop with a repeated beat and no words.
premises.why_send_it: Sent to a friend as a mood clip.
premises.rejected_because: silence leaves the verdict format and the wrongness illegible to a cold viewer

production_format.camera_style: Locked-off window-seat portrait; first and last frames identical.
production_format.rationale: A silent loop tests the silhouette and the dial click alone, but the rule is hard to land without the spoken verdict.

hook_variants.first_frame: Locked-off seated-eye-level portrait outside a grey corner shop: Uncle Verdict centred in the mustard three-piece on the white plastic chair, serene half-smile, holding the wooden paddle with the dial already pointing at 2, a closed umbrella across his knees, a thin grey rain edge visible at the top of frame.
hook_variants.first_line_or_action: He turns the dial with one finger (exaggerated click) and holds the paddle to the lens; caption and voice: 'Umbrella. Two out of ten.'
hook_variants.rationale: The mustard silhouette, paddle reading 2 and closed umbrella read in one second muted, and the dark sky promises the contradiction, so anyone with an umbrella argument will want to send it.

hook_variants.first_frame: Tight on the paddle held up to the lens with the dial at 2 and a single wet drop landing on the wood, Uncle Verdict's calm half-smile soft-focus behind it, the closed umbrella resting on his knee.
hook_variants.first_line_or_action: A second drop hits his bald crown and he does not blink; the dial clicks down one notch toward 1 while the caption reads 'Umbrella: 2/10'.
hook_variants.rationale: The rain on the paddle and his unmoved face make the problem concrete in the first frame, though the tighter crop shows less of the silhouette than a full portrait.

hook_variants.first_frame: Full portrait: the white plastic chair unfolded alone on the pavement outside the corner shop, empty, with the mustard-suited man's loafers just entering frame as he carries the paddle in.
hook_variants.first_line_or_action: He sits, settles the paddle on his knee and slowly lifts a closed umbrella; caption: 'Rating things. Correctly.'
hook_variants.rationale: The empty chair and the deliberate sit-down are a curious setup, but the wrong take is not visible yet, so it is slower to read and less likely to be sent.

hook_variants.first_frame: Slightly handheld seated-eye-level shot outside the corner shop: Uncle Verdict on the white chair in mustard, paddle dial at 4, looking calmly just past the lens; a hand enters from the right edge holding a perfect, unmarked banana.
hook_variants.first_line_or_action: He eyes the banana and says, slow and warm, 'Banana. Four out of ten.' while a finger rests on the dial.
hook_variants.rationale: The perfect banana against a 4 shows the wrongness instantly and is easy to send to a friend with strong food opinions, but the second hand adds clutter to the stillness.

hook_variants.first_frame: Close seated portrait of Uncle Verdict with a caption 'Rate the banana' across the lower third, the paddle dial at 4 visible, the white chair edge in frame, and a yellow blur at the right edge.
hook_variants.first_line_or_action: He gives one slow blink, then turns the dial a notch down with one finger as the banana comes fully into view.
hook_variants.rationale: The caption invites the viewer to take part and the slow blink shows his calm, but the banana is only a blur so the proof arrives half a beat late.

hook_variants.first_frame: Wide locked shot of the corner-shop pavement: the white chair, Uncle Verdict in mustard with the paddle at his side, and a tilted banana hanging into frame from the top edge.
hook_variants.first_line_or_action: He raises the paddle to the lens without a word, the dial reading 2, and the caption lands: 'Banana. Final.'
hook_variants.rationale: Starting at the verdict makes a strong image, but it skips the setup, so the wrongness is harder to read cold and the rule feels rushed.

selected.rationale: H1 shows the full silhouette, the dial at 2, the umbrella and the rain edge in the first frame, so the rule and the coming contradiction read muted in about one second, and the on_camera_dialogue / single_take_static pair is not in the recent list. The trade-off against the runner-up (P4 with H4) is that the banana hook has a cleaner single prop but adds a second hand and a more handheld frame that dilutes the seated stillness.

evidence.originality: A confident wrong rating contradicted by the scene is a familiar deadpan-reviewer structure, and the 2-to-1 dial drop is a mild twist, though the unmoved man in the rain gives it some freshness.
evidence.hook: Frame one shows the mustard suit, white chair, paddle at 2, closed umbrella and rain edge, so the claim and the coming contradiction read muted, but the first 6 s is a long spoken line with little visual movement.
evidence.coherence: Claim, rain, passing dry umbrella, dial to 1, and 'Final.' escalate cleanly and pay off the logline, but the 2-to-1 drop is a small, easy-to-miss change and the unopened umbrella on his knees is never stated as the joke.
evidence.identity: Silhouette, face, costume and the unchanged half-smile are specified consistently across all three scenes and make a distinct, repeatable character, with serenity-in-rain doing real character work.
evidence.audiovisual: Lighting, foley, ambience, dial click and caption beats are specified per scene and match the action, though the dialogue is dense for the available time and the final hold plus 'Final.' leaves little room to breathe.
evidence.feasibility: One locked unit with no cuts is cost-appropriate, but rain building on the head, a dry passer-by umbrella entering at the edge, a readable dial turn 2 to 1 and lip-synced speech in one Mini render are high risk for artifacts and wrong dial digits.
evidence.grounding: Location, props and costume follow the stated bible and the negative constraints are respected, but the passer-by's open umbrella is listed as a prop from frame one while the scene says slabs are damp-free, and the bible rule itself is not quoted so the link is asserted rather than shown.
evidence.commercial_fit: It is brand-safe and shareable, with a clear comment prompt in the CTA, but there is no commercial angle and the argue-in-comments hook rests on a mild, low-stakes take about umbrellas.

creative.summary: A clean, well-specified single-take introduction with a strong readable silhouette and a payoff tied to its premise, but the joke is gentle and the dial change is small. The render risks are real: lip sync, a readable 1, and a stranger's umbrella entering on cue in one cheap unit.
creative.top_fix: Make the contradiction land harder and more legibly in the first seconds: have the dry umbrella and first drops arrive earlier (about 4 s) and make the dial drop large and unmistakable (for example from 2 to 0) so the wrong-direction joke survives muted and a failed digit render.
